title: Static Members, Extension Methods and Namespaces
summary: Static fields, properties, methods and constructors, static classes, constants and readonly fields, extension methods that add methods to existing types, namespaces and using directives, file-scoped namespaces, global usings, and organising a project into files.

cards.q: Why can a static method not use this?
cards.a:
It runs without an object, so there is no instance for this

A static method belongs to the class, not to an object, so `this` does not exist there at all (it is a compile error, not a null).

cards.q: What makes a method an extension method?
cards.a:
It is static, in a static class, and its first parameter is marked with this

The `this` before the first parameter is what lets you call `s.Shout()` as if it were the type's own method. The type itself is not changed or derived from.

cards.q: What is the difference between const and static readonly?
cards.a:
const is fixed when compiling; static readonly is set once at run time

Both are read-only. A const is baked in at compile time and limited to simple types; a static readonly field is set once when the program runs and can be any type.
